terra.problem: Saying 'not those folks' asserts that no Pharisees or scribes were present. The passage simply doesn't mention them.
The group-chat comparison doesn't match the action of traveling with a crowd.
The passage doesn't say whether anyone asked Jesus to show compassion.
The passage doesn't say the widow was walking behind the coffin.
The claim that Jesus says this elsewhere needs a reference. The explanation also calls the baker's choice a 'wrong scene.'
The text says the coffin bearers stood still, not that the whole procession halted. It also doesn't say Jesus was a stranger to them.
Papa Dorin's gold base is part of him; he isn't bolted to it.
The text says those carrying the coffin stood still, not that the whole procession stopped.
The passage doesn't say everybody else had given up on hearing the young man.
The passage doesn't say Jesus turned or that the disciples were there for a show.
Calling the event a show treats the funeral scene too lightly.
The passage doesn't say nobody in the crowd had a plan for what happened.
The passage doesn't say the widow walked behind the coffin or that her son was standing in front of her. It says he sat up.
The passage doesn't say the mother had no one else. It says she was a widow and the man was her only son.
Not everyone present walked out for the funeral. Jesus, His disciples and a crowd were approaching the town.
The passage doesn't say nobody stormed off, or give a reason why they didn't.
The joke doesn't make clear how a batch can be kept secret from a bakery.
The geographical claim connecting Judea and Jerusalem is outside this passage and needs a reference.
